field.label: Enable
field.help: Run the HA daemon on this node.

field.label: HA link interface
field.help: Dedicated point-to-point interface to the peer. It needs a different static IP on each node and is never put in standby.

field.label: Management interface (optional)
field.help: Stays up on the standby and is used as a secondary heartbeat path. It is also excluded from MAC sharing and config sync.

field.label: Automatic failover
field.help: The standby promotes itself when the active node is lost on all heartbeat paths, and a rebooted node waits in standby. Disable to fail over manually only.

field.label: Primary takes over again (preemption)
field.help: When the primary node is back as standby and the peer has been active and healthy for the delay below, hand the active role back to the primary.

field.label: Monitored interfaces
field.help: Comma separated interface keys (e.g. wan). If one loses carrier on the active node while the standby still sees link on the same port, the roles are switched.

field.label: Monitor critical services
field.help: Restart the packet filter and IPsec if they die on the active node; switch roles if that does not help.

field.label: Probe targets
field.help: Optional. IPv4 addresses (for example the upstream router) that the active node pings every 2 seconds. If none answers for the failure hold time and the standby has link on the same ports, roles are switched. Use addresses that only THIS node's uplink can lose; an outage upstream of both nodes cannot be fixed by switching.

field.label: Use a virtual MAC address
field.help: Shared interfaces get a generated MAC address (02:...) instead of the primary's hardware address, so replacing a node never changes what the network sees. Applies to interfaces when they are first shared (pairing or kit). Existing pinned addresses stay as they are.

field.label: Keep GUI logins across a failover
field.help: Copies the web GUI sessions of the active node to the standby, so you stay logged in after a failover. Sessions are only sent over the pinned HA connection and removed on the standby when you log out. Turn off if you do not want session data to leave the active node.

field.label: Failure detection time (seconds)
field.help: How long the other node must be silent on every heartbeat path before it counts as dead. Lower means faster automatic failover (1-2 s) but more risk of a needless switch on a loaded or flaky link. Same value on both nodes.

field.label: Failure hold time (seconds)
field.help: How long a health problem must persist on the active node before roles are switched.

field.label: Fencing command
field.help: Absolute path of an executable (owned by root, not writable by others) that is run before an automatic promotion, for example to power off the peer through IPMI or a smart PDU. A non-zero exit status or a timeout (30 s) cancels the promotion. Arguments: promote, peer address.

field.label: Notification level
field.help: Which events are sent to the webhook. Every event is written to syslog (tag hasyncd). For e-mail, add the "ha_status" check from the documentation to Monit.

field.label: Webhook URL
field.help: Receives a JSON POST ({time, kind, node, message}) for every event at or above the level.

field.label: Promiscuous mode on data interfaces
field.help: Needed on virtual NICs (Hyper-V, some virtio setups) whose driver does not reprogram its receive filter when the shared MAC is applied. Real NICs (Intel ixl, igb, ...) do not need it.

field.label: Promote on HA-link-only silence
field.help: Without a management heartbeat path, promote even if this node cannot prove its own HA link is healthy. Risk: both nodes active if only the cable is cut.

field.label: Peer port
field.help: TCP port of the peer link (mutual TLS), bound to the HA link address only. Must be the same on both nodes.
